title: Equilibrium cluster statistics of cooperative and anticooperative binding on finite one-dimensional rings
authors: Thomas Alfonsi, Jérôme Dorignac, John Palmeri, Nils-Ole Walliser
abstract: We study equilibrium clustering in a finite one-dimensional lattice gas of $L$ sites with periodic boundary conditions, as a minimal model for adsorption and binding on small ring-like substrates. Using a grand-canonical formulation with nearest-neighbor coupling, we derive exact finite-size expressions for the mean occupancy, the mean number of domain walls, and the mean number of clusters. Building on exact $k$-site correlation functions, we further derive expressions for the mean number of clusters of size $k$ and for two complementary size statistics: the cluster-size distribution, and the site-weighted cluster-size distribution. These observables characterize how spatial organization changes across attractive (cooperative) and repulsive (anticooperative) interactions, and highlight finite-size and parity-dependent effects of the underlying lattice, the latter being particularly pronounced near half filling in small systems. To access larger lattices without enumerating all $2^L$ microstates, we also develop a cluster-based combinatorial formulation in which configurations are classified by cluster counts and sizes, reducing the effective state space to a set whose size scales with integer partitions, $\approx e^{\sqrt{L}}$, rather than with $\approx e^{L}$. Taken together, our results provide exact benchmarks for finite periodic systems and suggest experimentally relevant cluster observables that complement occupancy-based measures of cooperativity, with particular relevance for binding on ring-like substrates for biological assemblies.
summary: This paper develops an exact theoretical framework to calculate equilibrium cluster statistics for particles binding on a one-dimensional ring. By analyzing cooperative and anticooperative interactions, it derives key observables like cluster size distributions using advanced combinatorial methods. The results provide quantitative benchmarks for understanding how local interactions dictate the global spatial organization of adsorbed species.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the equilibrium clustering statistics for cooperative (attractive) and anticooperative (repulsive) binding interactions.
main_result: Exact finite-size expressions are derived for key observables like mean occupancy, domain walls, and cluster size distributions, characterizing how spatial organization changes with interaction strength.
method: The analysis employs the grand-canonical formulation using both a transfer matrix approach and an advanced combinatorial cluster-based formalism to manage state space complexity.
model_or_system: The model is a finite one-dimensional lattice gas of L sites with periodic boundary conditions, serving as a minimal system for adsorption/binding on ring-like substrates. The interactions are governed by nearest-neighbor coupling (J) and an effective chemical potential ($\mu$).
key_observables: Mean occupancy ($\langle\varphiangle$), mean number of domain walls ($\langle Wangle$), mean number of clusters ($\langle Kangle$), cluster-size distribution ($P(k)$), and site-weighted cluster-size distribution ($Q(k)$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength (J) and chemical potential ($\mu$). Key regimes include strong cooperativity, strong anticooperativity, and the noninteracting Hill-Langmuir limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving exact expressions for finite periodic systems, utilizing a cluster-based combinatorial formulation to reduce state space complexity from $2^L$ to one scaling with integer partitions ($p(L)$).
figures_summary: Figures show contour plots of mean observables ($\langle\varphiangle$, $\langle Wangle$, $\langle Kangle$) versus interaction parameters, and parametric plots illustrating the dependence of cluster statistics on occupancy ($\langle\varphiangle$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives exact finite-size expressions for various correlation functions and observables using two complementary formalisms: a site-based transfer matrix approach and a combinatorial cluster-counting method. It analyzes limiting cases (e.g., $J 	o \pm\infty$, $J=0$) to characterize different binding regimes.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of exact, finite-size statistical mechanics results for 1D systems provides crucial benchmarks that can be compared against more complex simulations or experimental measurements in biological contexts.
